answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The garden multiplier is published, charged in anchor, and jade lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3255 identities would post 1873 proofs and burn roughly 73 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
